narrative.overview:
The statute is the workspace. Every extracted part of a norm is a highlighter stroke laid on its exact characters, the modality cue word is circled in pencil, and every norm is a numbered paper flag stuck to the right edge of the sheet. The interface around the law is a quiet office: white printer paper resting on a pale graphite desk, graphite ink, graphite controls.

Colour belongs to the law, not to the software. The highlighter pens carry meaning (who, does what, to what, for whom, under which condition, how much), so they are spent only where that meaning is being shown. Everything else stays graphite and grey so that a reviewer on a projector or a reader at a desk sees the marked text first and the chrome last.

Density is a working desk, not a landing page: a sticky 56px top bar, an article index on the left, the sheet in the centre and a norm card on the right. Serif speaks for the law and for page titles; sans speaks for the interface.
keyCharacteristics: White paper sheets with a soft, low shadow on a pale grey desk ground.
Six highlighter roles plus a neutral grey, always under ink-coloured text.
Paper flags that overhang the sheet edge and change colour with the review decision.
Pencil marginalia in italic serif, muted grey, rotated one degree.
Graphite buttons, graphite tooltips, graphite toasts.
Bilingual chrome (vi/en); statute text always Vietnamese.

rules.name: The Pens Belong To The Law Rule
rules.body: Highlighter colours appear only on statute text, the colour legend, role swatches and illustrative statute quotes. Never on chrome, navigation, avatars, buttons or citations.

rules.name: The Graphite Controls Rule
rules.body: Every control is graphite or paper. Green and red mark only a decision already taken (a pressed Approve or Reject, a decided flag), never an invitation to act.

rules.name: The Ink On Every Pen Rule
rules.body: Highlighted text keeps `ink`; colour is never the only signal, so every role also carries its name in the card, legend and glossary tip.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Serif is the voice of the law and of page titles; sans is the voice of the software. A control never sets in serif, and statute text never sets in sans.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Headings stand alone. No small label, kicker or uppercase tag sits above a title or heading.

rules.name: The Margin Earns Its Column Rule
rules.body: A statute unit gets a 150px margin-note column only when it carries a note; otherwise the text runs the full sheet width.

rules.name: The Paper Lifts, Chrome Lies Flat Rule
rules.body: Only paper objects and floating layers cast shadows; panels, chips, inputs and the top bar use 1px rules instead.

dos: Do keep every control graphite or paper; primary is solid graphite.
Do use green and red only to show a decision already taken.
Do keep highlighted text in `ink` and name every role in words alongside its colour.
Do mark citations with the graphite pencil underline, never with a highlighter pen.
Do give a statute unit a margin column only when it carries a note.
Do let paper (sheet, norm card) cast the sheet shadow and keep panels flat with 1px rules.
Do translate toasts at render time and clear them on navigation.
Do set the law in Source Serif 4 at 17.5px / 1.9 and the interface in Be Vietnam Pro.
donts: Don't put highlighter colours on chrome, nav, avatars, buttons or citations.
Don't place eyebrows, kickers or uppercase labels above headings.
Don't use coloured side stripes on cards, notices or quotes.
Don't colour an Approve or Reject button green or red before the reviewer has decided.
Don't add a seventh highlighter; new slot types share an existing pen (as party, condition and measure already do).
Don't cast shadows from panels, chips, inputs or the top bar.
